name: CaliQuake '97, Part 1
notes: The PPV's own music-video cold open bills much of the roster in passing (real-wrestler names and originals alike, most never individually minted); the first structured match is Sean Southward vs. a real-wrestler portrayal not otherwise tenured in this wing.

name: CaliQuake '97, Part 2
notes: Shane Douglas is billed as the reigning PCCW World Heavyweight Champion entering the show; the Owen Hart-under-mask reveal (El Jobbo Grande's opponent) is preserved in the served text but not separately minted.

name: CaliQuake '97, Part 3
notes: PCCW World Tag Team Championship: New Jack and John Kronus lose the titles to Pain & Suffering (Sabre and Sledge Hammer of the Danger Zone Alliance).

name: CaliQuake '97, Part 4
notes: PCCW World Heavyweight Championship: Tony Marconi defeats Shane Douglas, who is written out of PCCW in the same segment. JUSTICE (the Aerial Marauder, Law, Order and the Machine) attacks the new champion afterward in an angle that does not change the title.

name: CaliQuake '97, Part 5
notes: Main event: a Spin The Wheel, Make The Deal Texas Death Match, the Undertaker (an uncollected real-wrestler cameo, not tenured) vs. The Terminator, the former PCCW World Heavyweight Champion; closes with the co-FedHead's own administrative comments announcing PCCW's transition off its real-wrestler roster.

name: Jersey Jams, Part 1
notes: PCCW Extreme Championship: the Aerial Marauder retains against Raven with a surprise assist from World Heavyweight Champion Tony Marconi, who is revealed to have set up the Marauder rather than actually joined JUSTICE.

name: Jersey Jams, Part 2
notes: Pain & Suffering retain the PCCW World Tag Team Championship in a tables-strewn brawl against the Danger Zone Alliance's own rivals; John Kronus returns from injury to attack a former Eliminators partner.

name: Jersey Jams, Part 3
notes: Law & Order (two-thirds of the PCCW World Six-Man Tag Team Champions, JUSTICE) are billed against Murder Inc.; the Los Gringos Locos/Rick Rude angle closes the show.

name: PCCW Sunday Night for December 7, Part 1
notes: fWo (Face World Order) stable business opens the show; the World Television Championship program is set up for Ajax Shiva vs. Paul-Dog.

name: PCCW Sunday Night for December 7, Part 2
notes: Tony Marconi's own recorded comments on retaining the World Heavyweight title at Jersey Jams and setting up a rematch with Ajax Shiva.

name: PCCW Sunday Night for December 7, Part 3
notes: PCCW World Television Championship: Paul-Dog (fWo) defeats champion Ajax Shiva after interference from the Aerial Marauder.

name: PCCW Sunday Night

notes: CONFIRM-ONLY pass: this show confirms the wing's own continued 1998 operation under the same operators as the held 1997 corpus, credited on-screen as 'PCCW Productions'. Card carries a World Title match, a TV Title match and a Six-Man Title match (Law & Order vs. the Steiners vs. Los Gringos Locos), continuing the wing's own blended real/fantasy roster policy into 1998. Not structured into matches[]/characters, per this enrichment's own confirm-only tier; a fuller read of the wing's own January-February 1998 run (45 subject-bracket posts) remains for a future pass.
no_appearances_reason: Confirm-only enrichment pass; roster minting deferred to a future fuller read of this wing's 1998 run.

name: PCCW CaliQuake '99
notes: Parts 1-4 of an eight-part broadcast (the remaining parts do not survive in the held record). Sean Southward is billed defending a title already on file for this wing; JUSTICE, including the Aerial Marauder, opens a promo segment against a rival stable; the Terminator is billed heading into a Thundercage main event whose outcome is not shown in the surviving parts. The supporting roster otherwise turns over almost entirely from this wing's own 1997 holdings and is not individually catalogued here.
